connexion: Build a learning-augmented exploration policy that treats room-derived door locations as fallible predictions, combines concept-guided exploration with a bounded-budget fallback, and tests whether accurate priors reduce travel and validation cost while corrupted priors preserve a provable overhead bound relative to a specified prediction-free policy.
rationale: P supplies concrete semantic predictions and incremental validation loops, while Q supplies a framework for consistency, robustness, and prediction cost; investigation is feasible, but defining exploration completion, comparable fallback information, and safe switching requires additional modeling. The substantive local gain would be determining whether hierarchical room-to-door predictions retain useful guarantees when exploration itself changes their errors, with simulation under controlled prior corruption testing the proposed assumptions and benefits.
